tested_scope.candidate_mechanism: Use ChatGPT event-triggered Scheduled Tasks responding to Gmail, Slack, or GitHub activity as a purported Chat-native replacement for a Work-dependent monitoring/execution step.
tested_scope.scope_limit: This audit classifies only the event-triggered Scheduled Tasks mechanism. It does not classify ordinary clock-scheduled or monitoring tasks that do not use the event-triggered flow, and it does not classify a particular external mutation permission state.

primary_sources.title: Scheduled tasks in ChatGPT
claims_verified: The official page states that event-triggered (webhook-based) tasks run in Work and are created from Work.
The official page separately states that Scheduled Tasks support eligible ChatGPT models and that model availability and usage limits depend on task, account plan, and workspace settings.
The official page states that supported connected-app actions may require approval; if approval is required, the task pauses.

observations: The first-party product specification explicitly binds the event-triggered Scheduled Tasks flow to Work.
Therefore an event-triggered Scheduled Task cannot, by itself, eliminate a Work execution dependency under the current Phase-1 hard gate.

The same source also prevents treating generic Scheduled Tasks as quota-independent evidence by default, because task/model usage limits depend on plan/workspace settings; however this source does not establish that those limits are specifically monthly/trial/paid quotas, so no broader quota-failure classification is made here.
Approval language is conditional ('may require approval'), so this audit does not infer a manual-user dependency for every connected-app action; route-specific permission evidence remains necessary.

verification_result.reason: Official OpenAI documentation explicitly says event-triggered tasks run in Work, leaving a residual Work dependency. The current Phase-1 policy states that any residual Work step keeps the route unresolved and cannot pass.

checkpoint.exact_continuation: On the next primary_source_verifier invocation, verify one distinct currently proposed ordinary non-event Chat-native dependency-elimination route against its first-party product/tool specification and exact repository evidence. Prefer a route that claims zero-Work viability but still lacks a direct classification for permission/approval or finite plan/model usage-limit behavior. Do not re-audit event-triggered Scheduled Tasks unless the official specification materially changes. Preserve exact scope and reject any residual Work/protected-primary/manual-user step, finite monthly/trial/paid quota dependency, or nonzero incremental cost.
